hook: The spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhists, in exile since 1959.

pages.x: Lhamo Thondup was born in 1935 to a farming family in the village of Taktser, in northeastern Tibet.

When he was two, monks searching for the reborn Dalai Lama came to his house. According to Tibetan tradition, the little boy picked out objects that had belonged to the 13th Dalai Lama. He was taken to Lhasa and enthroned at four.
He grew up in the vast Potala Palace in Lhasa, studying Buddhist philosophy. He loved taking apart clocks and cars, and watched the city through a telescope from the palace roof.
In 1950 China's army marched into Tibet, and at 15 he was made Tibet's leader in full.
In March 1959, after an uprising in Lhasa, he escaped at night disguised as a soldier, and crossed the Himalayas on foot and horseback for two weeks to reach India.
He set up a government in exile at Dharamshala, in India, and tens of thousands of Tibetan refugees followed him there.
In 1989 he won the Nobel Peace Prize for seeking a peaceful solution for Tibet. He asks for real self-rule within China rather than independence.
He is known for his laughter and his love of science. He has said that if science proves a Buddhist belief wrong, Buddhists should change their belief.
In 2011 he handed his political role to an elected Tibetan leader. He has said that his own office will find the next Dalai Lama; China's government claims that right for itself.
The Dalai Lama has kept Tibetan Buddhism and culture alive in exile, and is admired around the world for teaching compassion and non-violence.
pts: Has led Tibetans in exile since 1959
